\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian norm moments]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianPi_norm_pow}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianPi_norm_pow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and every $k\in\mathbb N$, the function $x\mapsto\|x\|^k$
on $\mathbb R^n$ is integrable with respect to the product of $n$ standard Gaussian
measures.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian Fourier pairing]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing}
\leanok
For a real number $a$ and vectors $x,y\inbr^n$, the Gaussian Fourier pairing is the
bilinear form $-rac{a}{2\pi}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i y_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian Fourier pairing phase]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing_phase}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing_phase}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing}
\difficulty{3}
For any real parameter $a$ and vectors $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$, the Gaussian Fourier pairing
satisfies $-2\pi\,\mathrm{i}\,\langle x,y\rangle_a=a\sum_{j=1}^n x_jy_j$, where the
pairing is the bilinear form defined by the parameter $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian Fourier integral formula]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierIntegral_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierIntegral_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing_phase}
\difficulty{3}
For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $a\in\mathbb R$, let $H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$, and let
$x\in\mathbb R^n$. The Fourier transform of $H$ paired with the Gaussian Fourier pairing
of parameter $a$ equals its standard Gaussian integral against the character
$t\mapsto\exp\!\left(i a\sum_{j=1}^n t_jx_j\right)$; explicitly, it is $\int_{\mathbb
R^n}\exp\!\left(i a\sum_{j=1}^n t_jx_j\right)H(t)\,d\gamma(t)$, where $\gamma$ is the
standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Smoothness of the Gaussian Fourier integral]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.contDiff_gaussianFourierIntegral}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.contDiff_gaussianFourierIntegral}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierIntegral_eq, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianPi_norm_pow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a\in\mathbb R$, and let $H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be
strongly measurable almost everywhere with respect to standard Gaussian measure $\gamma$
on $\mathbb R^n$. Suppose there is a real constant $C$ such that $\|H(t)\|\le C$ for
every $t\in\mathbb R^n$. Then the function of $x\in\mathbb R^n$ given by $\int_{\mathbb
R^n}\exp\!\left(i a\sum_{j=1}^n t_jx_j\right)H(t)\,d\gamma(t)$ is infinitely
continuously differentiable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Characteristic function of a Gaussian vector]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_exp_mul_I_gaussianPi}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_exp_mul_I_gaussianPi}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.charFunDual_gaussianPi}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $a\in\mathbb R^n$. If $X$ has the product
standard Gaussian law on $\mathbb R^n$, then $\mathbb E[e^{i\sum_i
a_iX_i}]=\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_i a_i^2\right)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of a Gaussian Fourier integral]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianFourierIntegral}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianFourierIntegral}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierIntegral_eq, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierPairing}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a\in\mathbb R$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be
integrable with respect to standard Gaussian measure. The function sending $x\in\mathbb
R^n$ to $\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{i a\langle t,x\rangle} f(t)\,d\gamma(t)$ is continuous.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Norm bound for a Gaussian Fourier integral]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_gaussianFourierIntegral_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_gaussianFourierIntegral_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianFourierIntegral_eq}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $a\in\mathbb R$, $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$, and
$x\in\mathbb R^n$. With $\gamma$ denoting standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$,
one has
\[
\left\|\int e^{i a\sum_{j=1}^n t_jx_j}f(t)\,d\gamma(t)\right\|
\leq \int\|f(t)\|\,d\gamma(t).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Gaussian phase]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase}
\leanok
For a real number $a$ and vectors $x,y\inbr^n$, define the Gaussian phase to be
$\expigl(i a\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}x_i y_iigr)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Unit modulus of the Gaussian phase]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_gaussianPhase}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_gaussianPhase}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, every $a\in\mathbb R$, and every $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$, the
complex phase $\exp\!\left(i a\sum_{j=1}^n x_jy_j\right)$ has modulus $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Multiplication of Gaussian phases]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a,b\in\mathbb R$, and let $t,x,y\in\mathbb R^n$.
Define $\Phi_c(u,v)=\exp\left(i c\sum_{j=1}^n u_jv_j\right)$ for real $c$ and vectors
$u,v\in\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[\Phi_a(t,x)\Phi_b(y,t)=\Phi_1(ax+by,t).\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a double Gaussian phase]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussian_double_phase}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussian_double_phase}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_gaussianPhase}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $a,b\in\mathbb R$, let $x\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable under the product standard Gaussian measure $\gamma^n$.
For $u,w\in\mathbb R^n$, set $\Phi_t(u,w)=\exp\bigl(i t\sum_{j=1}^n u_jw_j\bigr)$. Then
$(u,w)\mapsto\Phi_a(u,x)\Phi_b(w,u)f(w)$ is integrable, as a complex-valued function,
under $\gamma^n\times\gamma^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Double Gaussian phase integral]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_double_phase}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_double_phase}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPhase_mul, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussian_double_phase, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_exp_mul_I_gaussianPi}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a,b\in\mathbb R$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$
be integrable with respect to standard Gaussian measure $\gamma$ on $\mathbb R^n$. For
every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the iterated integral over independent standard Gaussian
vectors $t,y\in\mathbb R^n$ of $e^{ia\langle t,x\rangle}e^{ib\langle y,t\rangle}f(y)$
equals, as a complex number, the real integral $\int
f(y)\exp\!\left(-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n(a x_i+b y_i)^2\right)\,d\gamma(y)$.
\end{lemma}
